finding: Several new validator branches have no negative test, and one accepted input looks like a hole
why: Branches the diff adds are untested, so they can regress unnoticed: a non-mapping `transport`, `patterns`, `stage-map` or kind block; `edges`/`steps` not a list of mappings; `schema-version`/`record-version` as a bool or string; `includes` with non-string items; a role that is not a mapping; a collision under `transport` or a kind block (only stage-map and patterns collide in tests).
fix:
Add parametrized refusal cases for each of these shapes, plus `stage-map:
  review: []` (an empty list currently passes `all([])`, so decide and pin whether it is refused).
evidence: test_a_misshapen_pattern_is_refused covers only charter:7, roles as a list, unknown key `team`, `name: yours`, and an empty stage value; production lines `if value is None or not all(isinstance(item, str) and item for item in names)` accepts `[]`; `_pattern_fields` edges/steps/schema-version/includes checks have no test.

finding: An includes entry that is a mapping crashes the validator with a TypeError instead of a refusal.
why: The `includes` membership loop tests `entry not in known` (a set) before any shape guard, so an unhashable entry raises an uncaught TypeError; main() catches only ConfigError (afk-config.py:1482), so validate and every load caller get a traceback, not the 'must be a block list of pattern names' problem that _pattern_fields appended.
fix: Skip non-str entries in the includes loop, e.g. `if isinstance(entry, str) and entry not in known`, since _pattern_fields already reports the bad shape.
evidence:
Input `schema: 1
patterns:
  mine:
    includes:
      - a: b
` -> `for entry in includes if isinstance(includes, list) else []: if entry not in known:` with entry={'a': 'b'} -> TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'. The list-of-mappings parse is exercised by the edges/steps cases in TEAM_CONFIG, so the parser yields dict items. [also raised by: refactor-safety]

criterion: Acceptance: a stage-map entry is one pattern name or a list of names; refuse an entry that names no pattern
finding: An empty list passes as a stage-map entry
why: `names = []` makes `all(...)` true and the loop checks nothing, so `stage-map: {review: []}` reads cleanly with no pattern behind it. AC-062 and AC-032 require each entry to name a pattern.
fix: Add `or not names` to the shape check so an empty list is refused like a null or empty-string entry.
